tools.name: vision6_get_account
tools.description: Details of the API key this server uses: the scopes it grants (e.g. list.view, contact.create, message.edit, report.view) and its creation/expiry time. Use it to see why a request is refused. GET /v1/.

tools.name: vision6_list_lists
tools.description: List the account's contact lists with id, name, creation/modification time and notification settings. Filter by exact name. GET /lists.

tools.name: vision6_get_list
tools.description: One contact list by id. GET /lists/{list_id}.

tools.name: vision6_list_list_fields
tools.description: The fields (columns) of a contact list: label, type (email, mobile, text, dropdown, date ...), allowed values and whether they are mandatory. The lowercase underscore form of a label is the key used for contact values and filters. GET /lists/{list_id}/fields.

tools.name: vision6_list_folders
tools.description: List the account's folders (list folders and message folders) with id, name, type and size. Needed for the folder id when creating a list or message. GET /folders.

tools.name: vision6_list_contacts
tools.description: List the contacts of one list: email, mobile, subscribed/blocked status, active flag, double opt-in and the list's custom fields. Filter by email, mobile, active flag, creation/modification time or any custom field (`filters`, e.g. {"city":"Brisbane"} or {"source:ne":"promo"}). GET /lists/{list_id}/

tools.name: vision6_get_contact
tools.description: One contact by id within a list, with all fields. GET /lists/{list_id}/contacts/{contact_id}.

tools.name: vision6_list_messages
tools.description: List saved email and SMS messages (templates and campaigns) with id, type, name, subject and sender. Filter by type or exact name/subject. GET /messages.

tools.name: vision6_get_message
tools.description: One message by id. With include_content=true the HTML and plain-text body is included. GET /messages/{message_id}.

tools.name: vision6_get_message_sender_defaults
tools.description: The account's default from name, from address and reply-to, applied to new email messages when you omit them. GET /message-sender-defaults.

tools.name: vision6_list_reports
tools.description: Send reports for campaigns, newest first: message name, type, sent, bounced, opened, unique clicks, unsubscribes, complaints, total recipients and last sent time. Filter by message, type, test sends or creation time. Click and domain breakdowns are only returned when requested via `fields`. GET /rep

tools.name: vision6_get_report
tools.description: One send report by id with all delivery and engagement counts, per-link click counts and recipient domain distribution. Optionally includes A/B test results and social click/share statistics. GET /reports/{report_id}.

tools.name: vision6_list_sent_contacts
tools.description: The contacts one message was sent to, with send time, first/last open time and open type (html, text, sms or not_opened). Use it to see who opened a campaign. GET /messages/{message_id}/sent-contacts.

tools.name: vision6_list_transactional_groups
tools.description: Transactional send groups (one per group name used with vision6_send_transactional) with sent, failed, bounced, delivered, opened, clicked and unsubscribed counts. GET /transactional-groups.

tools.name: vision6_get_transactional_group
tools.description: One transactional group by id with its delivery statistics. GET /transactional-groups/{group_id}.

tools.name: vision6_create_contact
tools.description: WRITE: add one contact to a list (needs an email and/or mobile that matches a field of the list). May trigger the list's 'contact created' automations and notification emails. Returns the new contact. POST /lists/{list_id}/contacts.

tools.name: vision6_add_contacts
tools.description: WRITE: add up to 200 contacts to a list in one request (faster than one by one). Each needs an email and/or mobile. Vision6 returns no contact data (HTTP 204), so use vision6_list_contacts to read them back. May trigger automations. POST /lists/{list_id}/contacts.

tools.name: vision6_update_contact
tools.description: WRITE: change one contact's email, mobile, custom field values, subscription status (email_subscribed/mobile_subscribed=false unsubscribes), active flag or double opt-in. Only the fields you pass change. May trigger 'contact updated' automations. Returns the updated contact. PATCH /lists/{list_id}/c

tools.name: vision6_delete_contact
tools.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE: permanently delete one contact from a list (for example for a privacy erasure request). To stop emailing someone but keep the record, use vision6_update_contact with email_subscribed=false instead. Pass confirm=true only after the user agreed to the deletion. DELETE /lists/{list

tools.name: vision6_create_list
tools.description: WRITE: create a new, empty contact list inside a list folder (see vision6_list_folders with type list). Returns the new list. POST /lists.

tools.name: vision6_create_message
tools.description: WRITE: save a new email or SMS message in Vision6. This only stores the message; it is NOT sent (use the Vision6 app to send a campaign, or vision6_send_transactional for a one-off send). Email needs email_type, subject and matching body fields (plain: content_text; html: content_html; plain-html: b

tools.name: vision6_update_message
tools.description: WRITE: change a saved message's name, subject, sender, folder or body. Only the fields you pass change. It does not send anything. PATCH /messages/{message_id}.

tools.name: vision6_send_transactional
tools.description: WRITE: SENDS REAL EMAIL OR SMS to the recipients immediately (asynchronously) and USES ACCOUNT SENDING CREDITS. It cannot be recalled. Up to 100 recipients per call, each identified by exactly one of contact_id, email or mobile, plus optional personalisation values (wildcards %%key%% in the body). E

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "vision6_send_transactional" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, always). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: vision6_get_account, vision6_list_lists, vision6_list_list_fields, vision6_list_folders, vision6_list_contacts, vision6_list_messages, vision6_get_message, vision6_get_message_sender_defaults, vision6_list_reports, vision6_list_sent_contacts, vision6_create_contact, vision6_add_contacts, vision6_create_list · Private data: vision6_get_account, vision6_list_lists, vision6_get_list, vision6_list_list_fields, vision6_list_contacts, vision6_get_contact, vision6_list_sent_contacts, vision6_create_contact, vision6_add_contacts, vision6_update_contact, vision6_delete_contact, vision6_create_list · Public sink: vision6_list_list_fields, vision6_list_contacts, vision6_list_messages, vision6_get_message_sender_defaults, vision6_list_reports, vision6_get_report, vision6_list_sent_contacts, vision6_list_transactional_groups, vision6_create_contact, vision6_add_contacts, vision6_update_contact, vision6_create_list, vision6_create_message, vision6_update_message, vision6_send_transactional · Destructive: vision6_delete_contact, vision6_create_message.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
